chunks: 4334 - It is narrated from Jamil ibn Salih, who said:

I had a female slave in al-Madinah whose menstruation had ceased, so I made a vow upon myself for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that if she menstruated. Then I came to know afterward that she had menstruated before I made the vow upon myself, so I wrote to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام while I was in al-Madinah.
So he replied to me: “If she had menstruated before the vow, then there is no vow upon you; and if she had menstruated after the vow, then it is upon you.”

key_terms.فَلَا نَذْرَ عَلَيْكَ: there is no binding vow upon you
key_terms.نَذْرًا: a vow made binding upon oneself for Allah

ai.seo_question: Is a vow binding if the event already happened before the vow was made?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that a nadhr (vow) is only binding if the condition it is tied to occurs after the vow is made. If the condition had already occurred beforehand, then no vow is due. It is a jurisprudential ruling concerning the validity and enforceability of vows.
